policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'had seen that some of his disciples ate their bread' renders the finite ἐσθίουσιν governed by ὅτι, not RP's participial ἐσθίοντας that feeds the added ἐμέμψαντο, so r02 is excluded; r00-base and r01 are the same words and differ only in punctuation, which the English cannot distinguish.
'their bread' renders ἄρτους with or without the article; ASV supplies the possessive either way and English cannot show the Greek article.
ASV's sentence ends at 'unwashen, hands' with no 'they found fault', so the added ἐμέμψαντο of r01 is not rendered.

'when they come from the marketplace' is the ordinary English of ἀπ᾽ ἀγορᾶς with a supplied verb of coming as much as of the added ὅταν ἔλθωσιν; the ASV wording does not distinguish, and no note is mapped here.
The mapped note 'Greek baptize. Some ancient authorities read sprinkle themselves' puts βαπτίσωνται in the ASV text and ῥαντίσωνται (r01) in the margin.
The mapped textual note 'Many ancient authorities add and couches' shows the ASV text lacks καὶ κλινῶν, and the verse ends at 'brasen vessels'.
ASV opens 'And the Pharisees and the scribes ask him' with a bare connective; RP's Ἔπειτα would give a temporal 'Then/Afterward', which the ASV does not render.
Pure Greek word order between negative, verb and subject; 'Why walk not thy disciples' renders either arrangement.
ASV reads 'defiled hands' with the margin 'Or, common' — its rendering pair for κοινός here and in v.2 — whereas ἀνίπτοις is rendered 'unwashen' in v.2.
ASV has plain 'And he said unto them' with no 'answering/answered' for the added ἀποκριθεὶς.
ASV renders the indirect object, 'he said unto them'; r01 replaces αὐτοῖς with ὅτι and leaves nothing for 'unto them'.
The candidates differ only over a recitative ὅτι introducing direct speech, which the ASV leaves untranslated in either case.
ASV begins 'Ye leave the commandment of God' with no causal 'for'; the added γάρ is unrendered.
The ASV verse ends at 'the tradition of men' with nothing for the added washings of pots and cups and many other such like things ye do.
'that ye may keep your tradition' renders τηρήσητε; στήσητε would be 'establish/set up', which the ASV does not say.
ASV v.12 opens 'ye no longer suffer him' with no connective for RP's added καί.
'his father' is the ordinary English of the articular τῷ πατρὶ as much as of πατρὶ αὐτοῦ; the possessive is unmarked and does not distinguish.
'his mother' renders the articular μητρί as readily as μητρὶ αὐτοῦ; the English possessive does not distinguish.
ASV 'called to him the multitude again' renders πάλιν; RP's πάντα would give 'all the multitude', which the ASV does not have.
Aorist and present imperative of ἀκούω alike yield ASV's 'Hear me all of you'.
σύνετε and συνίετε are alternative forms of the same imperative, both rendered 'understand'.
Word order of infinitive and pronoun only; 'can defile him' renders either.

ASV 'the things which proceed out of the man' renders ἐκ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου, not RP's ἀπ᾽ αὐτοῦ 'from him', so r02 is excluded; 'are those that defile' renders ἐστιν τὰ κοινοῦντα equally with or without the added ἐκεῖνά.
The note mapped at v.17, 'Many ancient authorities insert verse 16 If any man hath ears to hear, let him hear', places that clause outside the ASV text.
English 'into the house' takes its article from idiom; εἰς οἶκον and εἰς τὸν οἶκον are not distinguished by it.
ASV 'asked of him the parable' makes the parable the direct object; RP's περὶ τῆς παραβολῆς would give 'concerning the parable'.
ASV 'This he said, making all meats clean' takes the masculine καθαρίζων with the speaker; the neuter καθαρίζον would attach the cleansing to the preceding clause.

ASV lists 'fornications, thefts, murders, adulteries', the order of πορνεῖαι κλοπαί φόνοι μοιχεῖαι, which excludes RP's reversed sequence; r00-base and r01 are the same sequence differing only in punctuation.
ASV's opening 'And from thence he arose' is its usual rendering of either δέ or καί; the connective does not distinguish.
ὅρια and μεθόρια are both rendered 'borders'.
ASV text reads 'the borders of Tyre and Sidon' with the note 'Some ancient authorities omit and Sidon', so καὶ Σιδῶνος stands in the text.
ASV 'But straightway a woman ... having heard of him' renders ἀλλ᾽ εὐθὺς ἀκούσασα; RP's Ἀκούσασα γὰρ would give a causal 'For ... having heard' with no 'straightway'.
Word order of ἡ γυνή, δέ and ἦν only; 'Now the woman was a Greek' renders any of the three.
ASV 'And he said unto her' has the pronoun and καί; RP's Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν would name Jesus and give an adversative.
Word order of ἐστιν and καλόν only; 'it is not meet' renders either.
Word order of infinitive and dative only; 'cast it to the dogs' renders either.
ASV 'Yea, Lord' renders Ναί κύριε; the base has no word for 'Yea'.
ASV 'even the dogs under the table eat' has no causal 'for' for the added γάρ; καί alone is rendered 'even'.
English requires a plural verb after 'the dogs', so it cannot show whether the Greek neuter plural subject took the singular ἐσθίει or the plural ἐσθίουσιν.
The candidates differ only in the order of τὸ δαιμόνιον and the prepositional phrase; 'the demon is gone out of thy daughter' follows English order under all three.
ASV 'found the child laid upon the bed, and the demon gone out' has παιδίον ('child', not RP's θυγατέρα 'daughter') and the base order, with the demon clause last.
ASV 'from the borders of Tyre, and came through Sidon unto the sea' renders ἦλθεν διὰ Σιδῶνος εἰς; RP would give 'of Tyre and Sidon he came to' with Sidon in the borders and no 'through'.
English joining of two descriptions requires 'and' whether or not the Greek has καί between κωφόν and μογιλάλον.
μογιλάλον and μογγιλάλον are spellings of one word, rendered 'had an impediment in his speech'.
ASV 'And his ears were opened' has nothing for the added εὐθέως, which the ASV elsewhere renders 'straightway'.
ἠνοίγησαν and διηνοίχθησαν are both rendered 'were opened'.
λέγωσιν and εἴπωσιν are alike rendered 'that they should tell no man'.
English supplies the subject pronouns 'he' and 'they' regardless, so it shows neither the emphatic αὐτοί of the base nor RP's αὐτός; r00-base and r01 differ only in punctuation.
'the deaf' is generic English idiom and does not show whether the Greek had the article τούς.
